newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Swiss Re sees Asia as major growth market.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re sees Asia as major growth market.

text.p: Insurance premiums in Asia will grow at 2-1/2 times the rate of those in the rest of the world between now and 2000, said a new report received by Reuters on Wednesday.
The figures were published in a report by Sigma, the research arm of Swiss Re, the world's second largest reinsurer.
"Real premium growth of more than 10 percent annually", in Asia is predicted by the report, compared with "a global average of approximately four percent".

Sigma said insurance growth would reflect the rapid general economic expansion of Asia in the world market: "In the insurance industry, growth rates will turn out even more in favour of Asia since several countries in this region still have pent-up demand," it said.

This demand resulted from a per-capita insurance spend below that of the world average compared to income, said the report. "Only Thailand, Malaysia and South Korea are above the expected world average for premium penetration," it said.
The study covered China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.
Non-life business will be the main area of expansion, said Sigma, as Asia generates less than one fifth of the world total.
"This is surprising since most Asian countries are hit frequently by natural catastrophes (earthquakes, storms and flooding)," the report said.
In life business though "penetration is already above the world average and nearing saturation point", said the report.

Annual insurance growth to 2000 will be slower in Japan than in its Asian counterparts (at 4.3 percent in non-life and 3.5 percent in life) while Thailand will grow fastest in non-life (18.6 percent) and China will lead in life (25 percent), the report predicted.
